turns.content: A 125-by-8 rectangle is tiled by unit squares. How many interior vertical and horizontal gridlines does the tiling contain?

Place the relevant pair of corners in coordinates using the dimensions currently specified. Use the greatest common divisor of the coordinate differences to decide whether the segment passes through an interior lattice point.
Derive a formula for the number of 2-by-2 squares crossed by a corner-to-corner diagonal of an m-by-n unit-square grid, accounting for simultaneous gridline crossings.
Apply that formula to the current construction and compute the exact number of tile interiors crossed.
Perform an internal check of the numerical result using only the method and conventions established above.
Let n denote the number of 2-by-2 squares crossed in the 125-by-8 rectangle, despite the original tiling into 1000 unit squares. State n and the counting argument.
